title: Kakatiya Dynasty
capsule: The Kakatiyas were a Telugu dynasty who ruled from Warangal (Orugallu) in the Deccan, beginning as Rashtrakuta subordinates before asserting independence under Prola II in the mid-twelfth century and reaching their apex under Queen Rudrama Devi (r. c. 1263–89) and her grandson Prataparudra II. The kingdom controlled much of what is now Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, building the great Warangal Fort and the Thousand-Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda, and promoted Telugu literature and tank-based irrigation. Prataparudra II resisted three earlier Delhi Sultanate invasions before Ulugh Khan — the future Muhammad bin Tughluq — defeated and captured him in 1323, ending the dynasty and incorporating its territories into the sultanate.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Kakatiya core in Telangana is well attested through extensive Telugu epigraphy; outer zones of tribute collection are inferred from copper-plate grants and are less precisely mapped.
